summary: Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar. He has served on the faculty at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in 2000 and faculty in 2026.

Benjamin Goldstein works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.
Benjamin Luk Williams works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 2017 and held a post at Naropa University.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University and Harvard University (circa 1991–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.

Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke (2011), and Thupten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1915). He taught at Taisho, Nihon, and Waseda universities, became president of Tokai Gakuen Junior College (1963), and directed Sanko Library and Sanko Research Institute.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Calcutta (~1917–1919) and a doctorate from the University of Dhaka (~1922–1925), later serving as Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1927).

Benoît Vermander specializes in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres, he served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became professor of religious sciences at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Sciences Po, Paris Diderot University, and under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida. His posts include Cornell University (~1983–1987), Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank (1927–1996) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, studying under Rolf Alfred Stein (~1950–1956). He was director at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Japanese civilization at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian and archaeologist. He held posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1992–1998) and Heidelberg University (around 2003).

Bernfried Schlerath (1924–2003) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1953–1956) and held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1956–1968), the University of Marburg, and Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer (1894–1947) was an Indology scholar who succeeded Heinrich Lüders. He held a professorship at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1935 to 1945.

Bernhard Forssman is an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1961–1964), later holding posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger (1881–1964) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Vienna, Bonn, Charles, Göttingen, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel (1807–1847) was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1829–1832), Göttingen (~1832–1833), and Paris (~1833–1834). He held posts as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Karlgren (1889–1978) was a scholar in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915), where he also held a post (~1915–1918), before holding an academic position at the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver (1938–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, and occupied chairs of Indology at Kiel (1974–1993) and Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman (1939–2018) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at NYU, Brooklyn Poly, and UCLA, and trained under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka, later founding the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.
